# 1 Samuel Chapter 12 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 167r–167v | **Source Image:** 1SA_012_page_001.jpg, 1SA_012_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Samuel addressed all Israel: "I have listened to everything you said to me, and I have set a king over you.

**2** Now you have a king to lead you. As for me — I am old and gray, and my sons are here among you. I have walked before you from my youth until this very day.

**3** Here I stand. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed: Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I cheated? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I accepted a bribe to look the other way? Tell me, and I will make it right."

**4** They answered, "You have not cheated us. You have not oppressed us. You have never taken anything from anyone's hand."

**5** He said to them, "The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness today, that you have found nothing in my hands." They replied, "He is witness."

**6** Then Samuel said to the people, "It is the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron and who brought your ancestors up out of the land of Egypt.

**7** Now take your stand, so I can lay before you the evidence — all the righteous acts the LORD has done for you and your ancestors.

**8** When Jacob went to Egypt and your ancestors cried out to the LORD, the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought them out of Egypt and settled them in this place.

**9** But they forgot the LORD their God, so he handed them over to Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army, and to the Philistines, and to the king of Moab, who fought against them.

**10** They cried out to the LORD and said, 'We have sinned! We have abandoned the LORD and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth. But now rescue us from our enemies, and we will serve you.'

**11** So the LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and he delivered you from the enemies all around you, and you lived in safety.

**12** But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites was marching against you, you said to me, 'No — we want a king to rule over us!' — even though the LORD your God was already your king.

**13** Now here is the king you have chosen, the one you demanded. The LORD has placed a king over you.

**14** If you fear the LORD, serve him, obey his voice, and do not rebel against his commands — if both you and the king who reigns over you follow the LORD your God — good!

**15** But if you do not obey the LORD's voice and instead rebel against his commands, then the LORD's hand will be against you, as it was against your ancestors.

**16** Now stand still and witness the great thing the LORD is about to do before your eyes.

**17** Is it not wheat harvest right now? I will call on the LORD to send thunder and rain. Then you will see and understand how great an evil you committed in the LORD's sight by demanding a king."

**18** Samuel called on the LORD, and that very day the LORD sent thunder and rain. All the people were terrified of the LORD and of Samuel.

**19** They all pleaded with Samuel, "Pray to the LORD your God for your servants, so that we will not die! For we have added to all our other sins this evil of demanding a king."

**20** Samuel answered the people, "Do not be afraid. Yes, you have done all this evil. But do not turn away from the LORD. Serve the LORD with all your heart.

**21** Do not turn aside after worthless things that can neither help nor rescue you, because they are nothing.

**22** For the sake of his great name, the LORD will not abandon his people, because the LORD was pleased to make you his own.

**23** As for me — far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. I will continue to teach you the way that is good and right.

**24** Only fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart. Consider the great things he has done for you.

**25** But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 3 — Samuel's integrity speech:** The Hebrew is structured as a legal trial. Samuel uses forensic vocabulary: "testify against me" (עֲנוּ בִי), "whose ox... whose donkey" (אֶת־שׁוֹר מִי לָקַחְתִּי וַחֲמוֹר מִי לָקַחְתִּי). He is asking the nation to serve as jury in the case of his own character. The specific items — ox, donkey, bribe — track Moses' own defense in Numbers 16:15. Samuel consciously patterns his farewell after Moses'.

**Verse 11 — "Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel":** Samuel includes himself in the list of deliverers without false modesty. "Bedan" (בְּדָן) is debated — some identify him with the judge Abdon, others with Barak, others with Samson. The Leningrad Codex clearly reads בְּדָן. The dynamic rendering preserves the name as given in the text.

**Verse 17 — Thunder during wheat harvest:** Wheat harvest in Israel falls in late May to June — the dry season, when rain is virtually unheard of. Thunder and rain at this time would be unmistakably supernatural. Samuel is orchestrating a theophany to prove his point: the God you just rejected as king still controls the very weather. If he can do this, why did you need a human king?

**Verse 22 — "the LORD was pleased to make you his own":** The Hebrew כִּי הוֹאִיל יהוה לַעֲשׂוֹת אֶתְכֶם לוֹ לְעָם contains the verb הוֹאִיל, which means "to be willing, to consent, to be pleased to begin." God's commitment to Israel does not rest on their merit but on his own sovereign pleasure. This is pure grace theology in the mouth of the last judge — even after their rejection of divine kingship, God's commitment to his name keeps his covenant intact.

**Verse 23 — "far be it from me to sin... by ceasing to pray":** Samuel defines prayerlessness as sin — חָלִילָה לִּי מֵחֲטֹא לַיהוה מֵחֲדֹל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּעַדְכֶם. This is a radical statement: intercessory prayer is not optional generosity but a moral obligation. Even though the people have rejected his leadership model, Samuel will not stop interceding for them. The prophet's vocation is not contingent on the people's obedience.

— PNEUMA
